property_summary: For any inputs where transfer(...) does not revert, the reference C always returns true; the mutant returns false for the same inputs, so there exists some input where the return value differs (reference returns true, mutant returns false).

For any inputs, the reference contract returns true whenever at least one low-level call to the external caddress succeeds (i.e., does not revert), whereas the mutant may return false if any individual low-level call fails (returns false) even though some earlier or later calls succeeded — the mutant can short-circuit and produce false while the reference still returns true.

For any inputs, the reference C.transfer(...) returns true if at least one callee invocation does not revert (since it ignores call return values), while the mutant that short-circuits on a falsy low-level call return can return false for some inputs where at least one callee succeeded; the property: for all inputs with non-empty _tos, calling transfer against a mix of a callee that reverts and a callee that succeeds never makes the reference return false (it always returns true), but the mutant can return false for some ordering — the test deploys a callee that sometimes reverts to expose this difference.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee address, the reference C.transfer(...) always returns true (it ignores low-level call return values and only reverts on empty _tos), whereas the mutant can return false if any individual low-level call returns false — so there exist inputs (a mix of callees that succeed and one that returns false) where the mutant returns false while the reference still returns true.
